title: NO SOAP REQUIRED. (it opens.)
format: carousel, 5 slides at 1080x1440: S1 video loop 10.0 s (frame 0 = the cover = the grid tile, soft baked foley), S2 video loop 8.0 s (silent), S3-S5 stills
date: Wed 28 Oct 2026 (Karwa Chauth eve; never dated on any image)
caption:
The night before Karwa Chauth, the bangle shop runs on soap, a plastic bag and the bangle-wala's faith that it will go on.

This one opens. The Silk Mesh Cuff is a rounded tube of fine woven mesh about 19 mm wide, ending in two polished caps that face each other across an opening of about 2.5 cm. In 18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated, ₹1,499.

Wear one on each wrist. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

[ silk mesh cuff · gold tone or rhodium · no soap ]
first_comment: Soap, plastic bag, or a very determined bangle-wala? Every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available #NairaFlore #KarwaChauth #CuffBracelet #DemiFineJewellery #NairaPetite
alt_text: An illustrated pink Art Deco shopfront with a sage board reading BANGLE STORES and the Marathi word for bangles. Inside the deep red shop, stacks of glass bangles hang on two rods along the far wall under the words NO SOAP REQUIRED. and 'it opens.' On the glass counter lies a gold-tone woven mesh open cuff, its two polished caps facing each other across the gap, and beside it a steel soap dish holding a pink bar of soap. The cuff catches one glint, the soap dish slides away along the counter, a warm light passes over the bangles and the dish slides back. A pink paper lantern hangs at the left and a brass plate reads SHOP 2.

Two blush velvet pads side by side on a glass counter in a deep red room, a gold-tone Silk Mesh Cuff lying on one and a rhodium-plated one on the other, under the words GOLD TONE OR RHODIUM. and 'same cuff, two finishes. one on each wrist.' A glint crosses each cuff in turn and a soft warm light passes over the velvet. Below: SILK MESH CUFF · EDITION TWO.

Close-up photograph of the cuff's two mirror-polished gold-tone caps facing each other across the opening, a small bracket marking the opening between them, and on the plaster block below the words IT OPENS., the note (shown larger.) and the line: opening about 2.5 cm, inner width about 6 cm, mesh about 19 mm wide.

Photograph of a woman's hand resting on her shoulder, the gold-tone mesh cuff open on her wrist, framed in a thin gold line on deep red, with the line '(on the wrist opposite your watch, as the listing says.)'

End card on blush plaster: a brass plate with the Naira wordmark, then SHOP 2 · GROUND FLOOR, SILK MESH CUFF, 18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated, ₹1,499, 'no soap required.', nairaflore.com, and every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available.
sound: Slide 1 carries its own very soft baked foley (peak -22 dBFS, nothing at the loop seam): one glass ting at 1.78 s with the first sparkle's peak (the moment the glint reaches the left cap), the steel soap dish sliding on the glass at 3.3 s (out) and 7.8 s (back), each slide's loudness following the move's own speed and settling with a soft knock. Optional in-app: a quiet santoor or sitar instrumental from the Instagram audio library, no vocals, ducked under the foley. Slide 2 silent.
deviations: Slide 1's loop starts with the soap dish OFFERED (frame 0 = the cover) and runs answer, not needed, the lamp passing, offered again: the brief's order, with frame 0 moved one beat. In an 840 px opening the 520 px cuff plus the 40 px halo gap leaves 280 px for the dish, so the brief's rest at the jamb (138 px showing) followed by a 300 px slide would have run the dish into the cuff. Now the dish travels the brief's 300 px (fully out and back) and the cover carries the soap whole enough to read in the grid. Beats: glint 1.2-2.3 s (LINEAR, see below), sparkles start 1.45 / 1.66 s and peak 1.78 / 1.99 s as the band reaches each cap, out 3.3-4.4 s, lamp pass 4.6-7.6 s, back 7.8-8.9 s.

THE GLINT (fix pass, review item 1): linear, not the kit's ease-inout, and its travel cut to the piece: the band's centre runs -0.15 W -> 1.15 W (background-position 82.5 % -> 17.5 % at 300 %), so the whole 1.1 s is spent on the cuff and each cap is lit for 6 frames (it was a 0.13 s crossing with a one-frame flash). Sparkles start 1.45 / 1.66 s, 0.03 s earlier than the review's 1.48 / 1.69, so their peaks (p .55 of 0.6 s) fall exactly at 1.78 / 1.99 s, when the band reaches each cap's sparkle point.

THE GLINT'S STRENGTH (review item 2): the review's stops .20/.38/.20 still lifted the left cap +.16 L when measured, so the band is softer and wider instead: a near-Gaussian profile about 140 px across the 520 px cuff (45.5-54.5 % of the 300 % background), peak .21 on slide 1. Slide 2 sets the peak per finish, measured on its caps: gold .13 (its left cap is darker than slide 1's and greyed to S .27 at .15), rhodium .19. Colours unchanged: ivory #FFF7E6 on gold tone, neutral #F4F2F0 on rhodium.

Cuff placed at tile img (142, 750) (alpha x 150-653, lowest point on the glass at y 1081), not x 230-750. Set scale recomputed from the live listing: 6 cm inner + 2 x 19 mm mesh = 98 mm across 503 px = 5.1 px/mm (the brief's 5.8 assumed a 15 mm mesh); the soap dish is 424 px of content (8 cm at that scale), not 464 px. The dish's silhouette is computed 40.0 px (2D) clear of the cuff's (p02/_build/layout.py).
Fact correction: the live listing (read from Shopify 26 Oct) says the mesh is about 19 mm wide, not 15 mm. Slide 3's foot line and the caption say 19 mm.

Caption: 'In 18k gold tone plated or rhodium plated' (the claims wording) for the brief's 'In 18k gold tone or rhodium'; 'across an opening of about 2.5 cm' for 'across a 2.5 cm opening' (the listing says about).

THE TUBE (review item 9): a front fixture as before (so it rides with the headline on a camera move and never strikes through NO SOAP; re-checked on a find at e .5), now hung just UNDER the slat on P1's lintel line: housing tile y 354-367, #FFFDF7 core y 356-366 (246-254 in cover.jpg; it was hidden behind the slat, only its #D8CFC4 edge showing as a grey line), a tight #FFF0DC glow round it and its light falling about 40 px down the wall. As in P1, a light source is not in its own shade: when lit it lifts the slat's shadow strip and the reveal's top band (h.set, g). The glow is a tight one plus a fading wash, not the review's single broad screen: one broad cream screen greyed the red under it to a pink haze, the same fault as the lamp.

THE BANGLE WALL (review items 6 and 7; fix pass 3, director's fixes 2 and 3): eight stacks a rod of thin glass rings seen a little from the left, THREADED (each ring's top 4 px above the rod's top edge, its far half behind the rod and its near half drawn again over it), each stack's shadow its own silhouette, blurred 4, offset +4 / +6, multiply 30 %. Now TWO rods, at tile y 698 and 768 (room 368 / 438; were 716 / 788 / 860). The bottom rod and its eight stacks are deleted: the C-HALO masked it across the whole opening (the hole's top contour runs only 6-15 px above it), which left three stacks hanging on nothing, a grey clip line through the lilac stack and a 38 px rod stub floating beside the cuff's right arm. Raised 18 / 20 px, the top row's rings end at y 744, 14 px clear of the cuff's top contour (758), so no stack touches the cuff; the middle row ends at 813, 23 px above the glass's new back edge; the ring tops at 689 sit about 27 px under the turn's descenders. Softened 0.6 px at 92 %.

THE COUNTER ON SLIDE 1 AND THE COVER (director's fix 1): the glass top's back edge moved from tile y 905 to 836 (room 575 -> 506; every y 575 in the counter layer, rect, gradient, both streaks and the two edge rects, now 506, height 195 -> 264). At 905 the back wall and three bangle stacks showed through the cuff's opening above the glass and the cuff read as hanging off the back of a 195 px counter. The opening's top contour is at y 849 or lower everywhere, so it now shows only glass: a wall-on vs wall-off render (stacks, rods, their shadows and the lamp layers hidden; p02/_build/holecheck.cjs + hole1.py) differs by 0 px inside the opening (28 776 px), and the wall's pixels end at row 826.

C-HALO ON THE RODS (director's ruling): the rods and their end caps are masked by the cuff's halo (00-trim alpha at 0.67 dilated 14 px, p02/assets/silk-mesh-cuff-00-halo14.png, p02/_build/halo.py with the shared recipe), the stacks are not. Re-measured with the two rods (p02/_build/rodcheck2.cjs + rodmeasure.py: the rods' own pixels, by a rods-on vs rods-off diff with the cuff, dish and stacks hidden): the nearest rod pixel is 14.04 px from the cuff's alpha. The bottom rod's special case (its left end behind the cuff) went with it.

THE LAMP (review item 8): rgba(255,178,110,.15) on the wall, not the review's rgba(255,206,150,.18) (that still took the wall to S .375-.43); +.08 L at S .47 between the stacks. A second copy masked to the rings at .30 (#FFD9AE) lifts the glass +.08 L as it passes. Fix pass 3: both re-clipped to the wall above the glass (P.passClip top 346 / height 160, the .p-glassband rect the same; were 350 / 250), so the pass ends at the glass's back edge and never lights the counter. Timing unchanged (4.6-7.6 s, linear).

SLIDE 2, THE CONES ARE GONE (fix pass 3, director's fix 4, option b): after two passes the drawn cones still read as upturned salmon plastic cups at phone size and were the largest shapes on the slide, holding nothing. Each cuff now lies on its own blush velvet pad CUT FROM AI-05 (P1's tray, kit/plates/AI-05-clean.png: its velvet floor x 560-1560, y 540-1040, high-passed so only its own nap is kept, the photograph's light falloff removed, mapped at about 0.66 so the nap shows at 1080), drawn as a rounded pad in the cuffs' own view (p02/_build/pads.py -> p02/assets/s02-pad-gold.png, s02-pad-rhod.png, p02/s02-pads.js): a rosier, slightly deeper tint under the shop's warm light, a soft pile sheen, the rolled front edge and the far edges a velvet sheen, an 18 px face darker toward the glass, the second pad re-cut from another part of the floor, never flipped. Option (a), generating AI-06, was not taken: this build's AI plates are not generated (credits; render/v3/README.md 'Textures and plates'), and a paid generation is the owner's call, not a fix pass's; option (b) uses a plate the street already shows.

SLIDE 2 PAD SIZE: 462 x 274 px each (top surface y 874-1124 plus the 18 px face; 446 px wide at the back), not the fix's 'about 470 x 190'. 190 px cannot hold the ring: the rhodium cuff's opening starts at y 888 and both cuffs' lowest points are at y 1100, so the top must run at least 212 px deep before any front margin, or the opening shows the pad's back edge. Measured (pads.py): every pixel of both openings lies on the pad's top surface, at least 15 px (rhodium) and 36 px (gold) inside its edges; each cuff sits at least 18 px inside its pad's sides. The pads are 13 px apart (cuffs unmoved at x 93-507 and 572-986). The glass's back edge moved from y 740 to 790 (the pads stand on it 84 px in) and the back wall carries a soft warm pool (overlay #FFC8A0 .34, centred x 540, y 760), so with the cones gone the wall between the turn and the counter is lit rather than empty.

Slide 2's contact shadows are retraced on the velvet (pads.py lines, multiply, clipped to each pad's top, in a deep warm brown #3A1411 / #4A1C18 so the velvet darkens toward its own colour and never greys): a tight core and a soft spread along each cuff's lowest opaque pixel per column (broken at the opening between the caps), the back tube's own contact seen through the opening, and a broad occlusion under the ring. The glass bounce under each cuff is dropped (velvet is matte). Each pad casts its own shadow on the glass: a hair of contact under its face, a soft spread and a broad one forward. The 5.0-7.0 s sweep (#FFE9CF, peak .26, screen) is clipped to the two pads, top and face, and laid before the cuffs: through it the cuffs' opaque pixels change by a mean of 0.00-0.01 levels; only anti-aliased edge pixels take the light. Glints unchanged.

Slide 3 (review items 5 and 10; fix pass 3, director's fix 5): '(shown larger.)' in Jost 300 20 ink soft, right-aligned at x 1008 on baseline 1250; the bracket label now reads THE OPENING (Jost 500 30 ink, tracked .08, centred under the bracket at the same position, about 34 px clear of either cap). 'ABOUT 2.5 CM' contradicted the slide's own scale: the 445 px cap is the 19 mm tube in the foot line (about 23.4 px/mm), so the 265 px bracket spans about 11-12 mm, and on the cover the caps are about 70 px apart at 5.1 px/mm (about 14 mm). The listing's 2.5 cm matches slide 4 (the cuff flexed open on the wrist), not the cuff at rest. 'opening about 2.5 cm' stays in the foot line and the caption as the listing's figure. OWNER, evening of 27 Oct, with the price and stock re-read: please measure the gap between the caps on a real piece at rest. If it is about 1.3 cm, the listing and every '2.5 cm' in this post (slide 3's foot line, the caption) change together.
Slide 4 crop is x 330-1060, y 490-1461 (30 px higher than the brief's y 520) so the hand is not cut across its knuckles; no higher, where a strand of hair enters the corner. Still no lips or chin.
Slide 5's fact line is Jost 400 28 ink soft at baseline 800 as the post brief specifies, in place of the kit end card's Cormorant line.

The brief names tools/loop.cjs: p02/tools/loop.cjs now only hands its old command lines to the shared feed/tools/reel.cjs --loop (series fix S3); slide 1 and the unsigned fallback are rendered by reel.cjs directly (node feed/tools/reel.cjs s01.html 10 s01.mp4 30 --loop --audio <previous s01.mp4>).

THE KANDIL'S LIGHT ON P2 (final render, 26 Oct; supersedes fix pass 3's mask): the bay no longer puts its own mask on the kit's halo, so the kit lights P2 exactly as it lights P1 next door (kit round 3: a soft pool on the sage, a soft glow + lift on every other ground, the red room included, no rim); the leak under the finial stays off (the director's fix-6 ruling: it sits almost wholly over the room). Why: fix pass 3 masked the halo to the plaster when the kit's light was ONE overlay disc of #FF7448 60 % on every ground (a saturated red disc with a rim on the room). The room light the director then accepted ((200, 420) to (132, 58, 50), 'its own red') came from the kit's glow, which the round-2 kit switched off for any bay with its own mask; so on the final world, with the mask, the lantern lit nothing round it but a faint wash on the pilaster (room and shutter dL* 0.0 at r 40-140), beside P1's warm pool. Measured without the mask (tools/haloground.py's own tests, kandil lit vs unlit at cover scale: p02/_build/final/tools/kab2.cjs + hg.py): 0 stain px; the room +11.4 dL* at r 40-100 and +6.8 at r 100-140, S .51 -> .47 (light, not a stain; mean #5B1E1D -> #7F352E), its rim at most 2.09 dE per 8 px, ending r 158; the fascia and shutter sage the same soft pool as P1's (2 138 vs 2 144 px tinted by dE >= 8, median #525A47 on both, rim 2.08 on both); the plaster within 0.1 dL* of P1's in every ring; (200, 420) is (132, 58, 50) again. The lantern's body lifts dL* +12.97, as P1's. For the world lead: kit/README.md's 'a bay that puts its own mask on .k-halo (P2)' no longer applies (no bay does), and sheets/halo-sage.json can list P2 with the others on its next run.

THE BANGLE WALL RIDES WITH THE FRONT ON A CAMERA MOVE (final render, 26 Oct; found checking the find and pull-back on the final world). The world lags each interior (parallax k 1.15) and counter-moves the cover words so they hold still against the front; P2's top row of rings hangs only 26 px under 'it opens.'. On a pull-back the room's lag (up to ~108 tile px) carried the rings up through the turn and behind REQUIRED.: P2's own pull-back 4.53-5.30 s (82 tile px over at 4.87 s), and in the SHIPPED reels P4 and P6 at 1.27-1.43 s with P2 lit and unveiled (27 screen px over, 6 frames each; P7 0, P10 / P12 clear). Fix, in the bay file only: the wall's layers (the stacks, the rods, their shadows, the lamp pass and its glint on the rings) take the words' own inverse (world.js: scale(1 / a) translate(-tx, -ty) about the interior's origin), read from the interior's transform when the world sets it (a MutationObserver: its records are delivered before the frame is captured), so only the counter, the cuff and the dish lag. Two masks inside the wall move WITH the room instead: the cuff's C-HALO (the rods stay cut back round the cuff mid-move) and a new counter-edge mask (the glass hides the wall behind it as it rises). Nothing changes at rest: slide 1 at 0, 1.78 and 6.1 s is 0 px different. Measured as captured (p02/_build/final/tools/reelgap2.cjs: one evaluate per frame, measured as the frame is captured): the turn-to-rings gap holds at 23.9-26.7 tile px on every frame of P2's find + pull-back and of P4's reel (26 at rest); 0 overlap frames on P2's test and in the P4, P6 and P7 reels. Left as is: in P2's own pull-back (no shipped reel makes it) the cuff's top arc comes up to the turn's line for a few frames at about half scale (4.8-4.9 s), and the counter rides over the wall's lower row mid-move (depth). For the world lead: a documented way to put a room layer on the front plane, as the words are, would replace the observer; the P4 and P6 reels pick the fix up on their next render (their current mp4s still show the old overlap).

FINAL RENDER (26 Oct, 23:15-23:56) on the final shared world (kit/kandil.js 23:09, world/world.js 21:32; READMEs 23:10): every file in post.json re-rendered from its HTML source, plus alt/ (the unsigned fallback). s03-s05 use no world file and came out byte-identical; s02 uses only kit/core.js (PSNR 66.5 dB against the previous ship: encoder noise). The previous ship is kept in p02/_build/prefinal/.

Cause, in kit/kandil.js (tick, the band): at a face-on pose (theta = 0 mod 60 deg, which ms 0, 1666.7 and 5000 hit exactly) both side facets pass cos(psi) > -0.02, the left side facet and the front-left one tie on the sort's min x, and the polyline is chained front-left -> back-left -> centre. On the page's own frames (lossless) the lantern's step out of frame 0 was the largest in the loop (0.823). Frame 0 is the wrap AND the cover, so the loop opened and wrapped on that twitch, and the cover and grid tile carried the bent band. The kit is shared and not this post's to edit, so world/bays/p02.js gains a tick that re-chains this bay's band after the kit's tick (kandilBand: the same points, back vertex outermost as the kit draws it at every other pose; checked on all 300 frames of both pages: it changes exactly frames 0, 50, 150, and no frame is left chained front-to-back). It is a no-op on a band the kit chains correctly, so it can stay when the kit is fixed. Every other bay's kandil still has the bug at its exact face-on frames (frame 0 of every loop and reel at phase 0): a kit fix is to chain the band by azimuth, or break the min-x tie toward the back vertex.
